turns.assessment: The simultaneous multi-service outage is an optical common-cause failure, not a svc240 client-port fault. On OMS S01->S20, even the booster input power was lost while all amplifier pump-current telemetry remained unchanged; this localizes the loss ahead of amp0 and rules strongly against a downstream span cut or amplifier pump failure. Complete all-channel loss, together with recent work at S01, is characteristic of the S01 OMS input patch being disconnected or broken.

proposals.rationale: E7 is the input patch for OMS S01->S20. Loss at amp0 input and every downstream amplifier input/output, with stable pump currents, places the failure before the booster. The hard all-channel outage and recent S01 maintenance strongly support a pulled or broken patch cord.

A hard ROADM port failure at S01 could suppress multiple channels before the OMS booster, but the documented input-port behavior is less directly consistent than a failure of the outgoing OMS input patch.
Contamination at the same patch is possible after maintenance, but it normally causes reduced power rather than the observed complete signal loss.
